item.title: Living in Arnold, Maryland: Your Complete Guide to Waterfront Community Life
item.description:
Welcome to Arnold, Maryland

Estimated reading time: 5 minutes

Your First Look at Arnold

Moving to Arnold means waking up to water views and ending your day with sunset over the Chesapeake Bay. This Anne Arundel County community sits on the Broadneck Peninsula, where the Magothy River meets the Severn River, giving residents boat access to the bay without leaving the neighborhood.

When I first toured Arnold, what struck me most wasn’t the waterfront homes or the proximity to Annapolis—it was how the community actually functions. You’ve got the Baltimore & Annapolis Trail running right through, which means you can bike to schools, shops, or even Annapolis itself without touching a highway. It’s one of those rare places where the commute might be a bike ride instead of a 40-minute drive.

item.title: Living in Deale, Maryland: Your Guide to Small-Town Chesapeake Bay Life
item.description:
Welcome to Deale, Maryland

Estimated reading time: 5 minutes

Your First Look at Deale

Deale is where the Chesapeake Bay feels like your backyard. This small community on the southern end of Anne Arundel County’s Western Shore has a population around 5,000-5,500 people, which keeps it from ever feeling crowded. The name “Deale” comes from the early settlers who established the area in the 1700s, and walking through town you’ll still feel that small-town rhythm.

item.title: Living in Fort Meade, Maryland: Your Guide to Military Community Life
item.description:
Welcome to Fort Meade, Maryland

Estimated reading time: 5 minutes

Your First Look at Fort Meade

Fort Meade is unlike any other community in Anne Arundel County. This isn’t a typical suburb—it’s a major U.S. military installation that also serves as a residential community for military personnel, Department of Defense civilians, and their families. The installation is home to critical national security agencies including the National Security Agency (NSA) and U.S. Cyber Command.

item.title: Living in Millersville, Maryland: Your Guide to Family-Focused Suburban Life
item.description:
Welcome to Millersville, Maryland

Estimated reading time: 5 minutes

Your First Look at Millersville

Millersville is what Anne Arundel County does best when it comes to family living—suburban neighborhoods with top-rated schools, parks that actually get used, and a pace that lets childhood happen at a normal speed. The community has grown steadily over the years, and it shows in the infrastructure: wide streets, well-maintained parks, and a population that feels established but still growing.

item.title: Living in Parole, Maryland: Your Guide to Annapolis-Adjacent Suburban Life
item.description:
Welcome to Parole, Maryland

Estimated reading time: 5 minutes

Your First Look at Parole

Parole is what happens when suburban development meets proximity to a historic capital city. Located right at the western edge of Annapolis, this Anne Arundel County community blends residential neighborhoods with major shopping centers, healthcare facilities, and easy access to both the city and the broader metropolitan region.

The population sits around 15,000-16,000 residents (based on 2010 census data at 15,922, with growth since then). While it doesn’t have a traditional town center, Parole functions as a well-developed community with everything you need within a short drive.

item.title: Living in Sunnydale, Maryland: Your Guide to Southern Anne Arundel Countryside Living
item.description:
Welcome to Sunnydale, Maryland

Estimated reading time: 5 minutes

Your First Look at Sunnydale

Sunnydale represents what Southern Anne Arundel County does best: peaceful, rural-style living with waterfront access and rolling countryside. While you’re still in Anne Arundel County with all the county services and schools you’d expect, Sunnydale offers a different pace than the more developed northern and central county areas.

This is the kind of place where you might see farm animals grazing on rolling hills, discover a local vineyard on your drive home, and spend weekends on the water rather than in a mall parking lot. It’s a community that caters to people who want county amenities without the suburban density.

item.title: Anne Arundel County Tax Guide
item.description:
Anne Arundel County Tax Guide

Understanding taxes in Anne Arundel County is essential for budgeting and financial planning. This guide covers property taxes, income taxes, sales taxes, and other tax obligations.

Property Taxes

Anne Arundel County Property Tax

County Tax Rate:

  • Based on assessed value of property
  • Rates change annually
  • Published each fiscal year
  • Different rates for residential and commercial

Assessment Process:

  • Property assessed annually
  • Assessment based on market value
  • Assessment notices sent annually
  • Appeal process available
